Hexagram 31, Xian: the character for feeling has no heart in it
The classic chose the word without the heart radical. Same family, and the missing radical is the doctrine.
Hexagram 32, Heng: lasting is a line that goes away and comes back
The bronze form argues against freezing. Four ways to fail at endurance, and the pivot is direction, not position.
Hexagram 33, Dun: moving your position, not running
The dictionary says migration, not flight. Grader: praise, timing, and emptiness.
Hexagram 34, Dazhuang: a ram, a fence, and the one carriage binding that is praised
Three characters for cart parts, distinguished once and for all. Strength attached to the part that carries weight.
Hexagram 35, Jin: the sun rises and the ten thousand things advance
The best dictionary gloss in the book. A hexagram named advance opens with a lord whose virtue is not pushing.
Hexagram 36, Mingyi: the light is flattened, not extinguished
Level, level out, wipe out, wound. And the choice among three benevolent men: to leave, to die, to become a slave.
Hexagram 37, Jiaren: a roof with a pig under it
Household order drawn as a bar inside a door, and the whole question of a household reduced to two sounds.
Hexagram 38, Kui: one eye in the character, two eyes in the meaning
Divergence where the only good fortune allowed is small. A cartload of ghosts, and then the bow is lowered.
Hexagram 39, Jian: six lines, one character
Every line contains the same word, and four begin the same way. Returning graded from praise to weight.
Hexagram 40, Jie: the cook who did not change his blade for nineteen years
The character is a knife opening an ox horn. Cooks who cut change the blade yearly; the one who finds the seam does not.
